Ticket #22 — Shared Document Permissions

Difficulty: Hard

Practice Metadata

  • Interview format: Engineering ticket / existing-code debugging.
  • Primary skills: permission revocation, grant precedence, security regression testing.
  • Expected duration: 50–60 minutes.
  • AI assistance: Allowed in guided practice mode for explanations, hypotheses, test ideas, and focused hints; the candidate owns and explains every change.
  • Candidate objective: Ensure a document revocation blocks existing grants and verify that explicit regrant restores only the affected user's access.
  • Interviewer evaluation: Problem decomposition, code navigation, root-cause explanation, incremental implementation, and test evidence. See the shared interviewer rubric.

Context

You maintain sharing for documents inside nested folders. A direct grant is on the document; an inherited grant comes from its folder or a parent folder. A viewer may read, an editor may read and edit, and the document owner may also share. Revocation denies a user access at a specified scope.

Practice report

Create folder root, its child child, and document d in child, owned by owner. Grant sam editor access on root and viewer access directly on d. Revoke sam on d, then ask for role("d", "sam") and read access.

Observation Current starter Expected
Resolved role viewer None
Read route status 200 403

The document revocation must hold despite the two existing grant sources.

Core acceptance criteria

  • A document-level revocation denies that user's document access even when direct or inherited grants already exist.
  • An explicit document regrant clears the revocation for that user and document.
  • Revoking one user's access does not change another user's resolved role.
  • The immutable document owner retains owner access.

Optional follow-ups

If the core regression is complete, discuss nearest-folder inheritance, folder-level revocation, grant ordering, or cyclic folder data. Clarify the intended precedence with the interviewer before implementing additional rules.

Out of Scope

Keep the existing grant/revoke APIs, role set, and folder graph. Login, organization-wide policies, new actions such as deletion, and redesigning folder storage are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the document revocation report and trace the resolved role to the route response. Add a regression test for a denied user with existing grants, plus a focused check that explicit regrant restores only that user's access. Explain which other user's state remains unchanged.
